text:
anya: Heads up — pelican14b-int4 canary on dedicated pool hitting OOMs ~14:10 PST, saw a couple in the last hour. pasting root error and short notes.

anya: ```
[2026-03-23 14:10:23] ERROR runtime: CUDA OOM when allocating 7.3 GiB (requested 7864320000 bytes) on GPU 0
  at alloc_device_memory()
  note: alloc pattern looks like transient spike after kv_cache warmup
```

sam: Can you paste the tracer allocation pattern and current config? which batch / max_new_tokens?

anya: batch_size=4, max_new_tokens=1024, prefetch=true, kv_cache=on. This was with the int4 qv2 build.

devon: That smells like fragmentation + kv growth. Long single-request gens (max_new_tokens high) + prefetch = big transient allocations then free -> slab churn. Hypothesis: allocation spike exceeds contiguous free block despite total free memory.

marco: Check slab freelist metrics: slab.free_frag_ratio and alloc_retries. If those jump during OOMs we have fragmentation. Also kernel scheduling/affinity can scatter allocations. Suggestions: lower max_new_tokens, reduce batch, disable prefetch for canary, try kv_trim or slot_compactor.

qa-ella: I can repro locally with `./canary_run --model pelican14b --quant int4 --batch 4 --max_new 1024 --prefetch` — repro in ~2 runs, same cuda OOM. attaching local run log.

perf-bot: Perf alert: 95p latency jumped from ~180ms -> ~420ms during spikes. Token cost +30% on affected runs.

anya: Proposed quick mitigation: roll canary to max_new_tokens=512, batch_size=2, prefetch=false, enable kv_trim_threshold=0.75, soft_reserve=0.12. Will apply to the canary only and re-run smoke.

sam: If that fixes it, we should set a short-term default for pelican14b-int4 to avoid customer-facing OOMs and file an eval for quality difference between 512 vs 1024. Also add a safety gate on prefetch for int4 quant variants.

devon: Agreed. Also add an item to run `heap-scan` / post-canary fragment analysis to make sure fragmentation isn't persistent.

anya: Applying patch now. Patch snippet:```
model_defaults:
  pelican14b-int4:
    max_new_tokens: 512
    batch_size: 2
    prefetch: false
    kv_trim_threshold: 0.75
    soft_reserve: 0.12
```

infra-bot: Deploy job started: deploy/patch-pelican-int4-3241598765 (CI OK) -> rolling canary 10%.

anya: :thumbsup: will monitor logs/metrics. re-running canary now.

anya: Update 3241599420: ran 40 canary runs after the change, 0 OOMs. 95p latency down to ~200ms. slab.free_frag_ratio peaked less and alloc_retries dropped to zero during the window.

marco: Nice. Please open a PR to make the default change and add a note in the model onboarding checklist about int4 prefetch risk and kv_trim knobs.

sam: Created INF ticket INF-4321 to make the default change, add guardrail, and create an eval comparing quality at 512 vs 1024.

qa-ella: Running evals now (bleu/qa/regression suite). will post diffs in this thread when done.

perf-bot: Cost delta estimate: -12% token cost on canary after lowering defaults.

anya: Leaving canary at 10% for another day, then will roll to 50% if no regressions. Thanks all for fast triage.
